channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Euro flatlines against Japanese Yen as intervention risks rise
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross holds steady around 180.25 during the early European trading hours on Monday. Japan markets are closed for a three-day holiday, leading to low liquidity. Traders remain on high alert for currency intervention from Japanese authorities to prop up the volatile currency.

item.title: Euro stays defensive vs USD amid geopolitical risks as traders await Lagarde's speech
item.description: The EUR/USD pair struggles to capitalize on Friday's modest bounce from the vicinity of mid-1.1400s, or the lowest level since late July, and edges lower at the start of a new week. Spot prices currently trade around the 1.1475 region and seem vulnerable amid rising geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens as US Dollar gain support on hawkish Fed outlook
item.description: USD/CHF gains ground after two days of losses, trading around 0.8230 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) gains support amid hawkish sentiment surrounding the Federal Reserve (Fed) policy outlook.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD consolidates near $66.35 at the start of the week
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades in a tight range at the start of the week near $66.35 during the Asian trading session. The white metal consolidates while investors remain focused on developments in Middle East regarding the oil supply and the United States (US) interest rate outlook.

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds firm on hawkish Fed outlook
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is gaining ground after two days of losses and trading around 100.30 during Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Holds comfortably above 0.7100 as bulls await Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts some dip-buyers following a modest gap-down open on Monday and holds comfortably above the 0.7100 mark through the Asian session.

item.title: Gold edges lower to near $4,350 on Fed hawkish stance, Middle East tensions
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) edges lower to near $4,365 during the early Asians session on Monday. The precious metal loses momentum amid escalating tensions in the Middle East and hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve (Fed) officials. Traders await the Fedspeak later this week for fresh impetus.

item.title: Canadian Dollar seems vulnerable near August 7 low amid sliding oil prices, trade tensions
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts some dip-buyers at the start of a new week, stalling Friday's modest pullback from levels beyond the 1.4000 psychological mark, or the highest since August 7. Moreover, the supportive fundamental backdrop backs the case for an extension of a nearly two-week-old uptrend.

item.title: Ukraine attacks on Moscow oil refinery in massive drone and missile attack
item.description: Ukraine carried out a large-scale overnight drone and missile attack targeting Moscow and the surrounding region on Sunday, BBC reported.

item.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi capital, thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport
item.description: Yemen’s Houthis said that they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital Riyadh with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of smoke were seen near the city’s main airport, the Guardian reported on Saturday.

item.title: WTI falls to near $93.50 as Middle East diplomacy hopes ease supply fears
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price continues its losing streak for the fourth successive day, trading around $93.60 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar languishes near two-month low vs USD as bears await break below 0.5700
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers for the second straight day and trades around the 0.5720-0.5715 zone during the Asian session on Monday, well within striking distance of an over two-month low set last week.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7487 vs. 6.7521 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7487 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7521 and 6.6951 Reuters estimate.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says had a very successful engagement with China on trade and AI
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke ahead of the US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping summit, saying that he had a very successful engagement with China on trade and AI, Reuters reported on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen bulls seem hesitant amid BoJ's dovish rate hike as Fed bets support USD
item.description: The USD/JPY pair attracts some sellers following a modest Asian session uptick to the 157.10 area and moves away from a two-week high, touched on Friday in reaction to the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) dovish rate hike.

item.title: British Pound slips as hawkish Fed outlook boosts US Dollar
item.description: GBP/USD inches lower after registering modest gains in the previous trading day, hovering around 1.3390 during Asian hours on Monday. The pair loses ground as the US Dollar (USD) holds ground amid hawkish sentiment surrounding the Federal Reserve (Fed) policy outlook.

item.title: Euro edges higher above 1.1450 despite Fed hawkish stance
item.description: The EUR/USD pair posts modest gains near 1.1485 during the early Asian session on Monday. However, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish hike and ongoing Middle East tensions.

item.title: Confirmed: PBOC leaves Loan Prime Rates unchanged in September
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced to leave its Loan Prime Rates (LPRs) unchanged on Monday. The one-year and five-year LPRs were at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively.

item.title: Fed’s Kashkari: Inflation is still too high in “all aspects” of US economy
item.description: Minneapolis Federal Reserve (Fed) President Neel Kashkari said that inflation is too high across all sectors ‌of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices, Reuters reported on Sunday.

item.title: US, China open high-level talks ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: US and Chinese officials began talks in New York aimed at clearing the way for possible agreements on trade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and critical minerals ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later on Thursday, Bloomberg reported on Sunday.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges lower as Fed hike bets grow ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades with mild losses around 0.7120 during the early Asian session on Monday. The US dollar (USD) edges higher against the Australian Dollar (AUD) as the US Federal Reserve (Fed) delivered a 25-basis-point rate hike and flagged more hikes in the coming months.

item.title: Qatar’s Prime Minister says Gulf states have to act together on Iran
item.description: Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, said Gulf states must work together to restore stability in the Middle East and help find a settlement between the United States (US) and Iran, Bloomberg reported on Sunday.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Mildly hawkish CBC but flows drive – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong highlights that Taiwan’s CBC kept its policy rate at 2% for a tenth straight quarter with a mildly hawkish tone, sharply raising 2026 growth and inflation forecasts while flagging sticky services inflation.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: CBC holds rates but flags inflation risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Henry Hao report that Taiwan’s CBC kept its policy rate at 2.0% for a tenth straight meeting, signalling a patient stance.

item.title: South Korean Won: Foreign equity flows keep KRW heavy against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes that the Korean Won remains under pressure as foreign selling of Korean equities persists and elevated US yields after the FOMC continue to weigh. Large-cap technology stocks are at the centre of outflows, though the broader KOSPI has held up.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Dovish BoJ hike weighs on yen – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Japanese Yen (JPY) is down sharply versus the US Dollar (USD) after a dovishly delivered 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike and Governor Ueda’s cautious guidance.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Strong NODX but USD still drives USD/SGD – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong highlights that Singapore’s August NODX surged 46.2% year-on-year, far above consensus, with electronics exports jumping on AI-related demand and broad-based strength across markets.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Bulls eye 0.7200 after 0.7100 break
item.description: The Aussie Dollar is poised to end the week on a positive note versus the US Dollar, up 0.21% as improved risk appetite keeps AUD/USD trading near 0.7124, closing near Friday's highs.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Pre-summit support and firmer bias – DBS
item.description: Chang Wei Liang at DBS Group Research highlights that USD/CNH is easing toward 6.70 despite a stronger Dollar, with the Renminbi (RMB) supported by a lower USD/CNY fixing below 6.76.
